title: A day of rest
hookLine: your sabbath: when, how, what instead
tomorrow: an emperor came to see the Guru. why did he eat on the floor first?

lines: WHAT IS A DAY OFF FOR?
cards: Ask a few friends what a day off is for and you'll get an argument. Recharge, so you work better. Do nothing, on principle.
Finally catch up on errands. The Bible gives the Sabbath commandment twice, and the two tellings don't give the same reason. In Exodus it begins: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.
In Deuteronomy, when Moses repeats the commandments to the people, it begins: Keep the sabbath day to sanctify it. Remember, and keep. Then each one explains why, and the explanations part ways.

teach.b: Exodus says: for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day. Rest here is holy time. You stop because God stopped.
The day is set apart, a piece of time that belongs to God.

Deuteronomy says something else. Your servants rest too, and your ox and your donkey, that thy manservant and thy maidservant may rest as well as thou. And remember that thou wast a servant in the land of Egypt.
Rest here is freedom. Slaves don't get a day off. Free people do, and they give it to everyone under their roof.
One side says the Sabbath is first about holiness: without the holy, it shrinks into a long weekend.
The other side says it is first about justice: a weekly reminder that nobody is a machine, and the worker rests as well as the boss. The rabbis refused to choose.
The Talmud teaches that remember and keep were spoken by God in one utterance, and on Friday nights the hymn Lecha Dodi still sings it.
That is why Shabbat is kept both ways at once: as holy time, with candles and blessing, and as a day of no work for anyone in the house.

how: Jews keep Shabbat from Friday sundown to Saturday night as holy time, with candles, blessings and prayer, and as a day without work for the whole household; the Friday-night hymn Lecha Dodi sings of 'remember' and 'keep' said as one.

games.q: what does “a day of rest” mean?
o: a weekend for catching up on chores and errands
a day to recharge so you can work harder later
one day a week set apart from work, holy and free

games.q: two reasons to rest: tap the pairs.
p: remember: God rested on the seventh day
keep: you were slaves in Egypt

s: the Sabbath commandment reads the same in Exodus and Deuteronomy
Exodus says 'remember' and points to creation; Deuteronomy says 'keep' and points to slavery in Egypt.
in Deuteronomy, servants and even animals get the day off
'that thy manservant and thy maidservant may rest as well as thou.'
the rabbis decided one reason replaced the other
the Talmud says 'remember' and 'keep' were spoken in one utterance.

games.q: your coworker says the Sabbath is only about worship and has nothing to do with workers. what's the best case for the other reading?
o: Deuteronomy grounds it in slavery: your servant rests as well as you.
Exodus says God rested because the work had worn him out.
the commandment only applied to priests working in the temple.
games.why: Deuteronomy's reason is freedom: you were slaves in Egypt, so everyone in your house rests. The rabbis kept that reason next to Exodus' holiness, not instead of it.

practice: Choose your rest day, and the hour it begins. Name one kind of work you won't do on it, the one most likely to creep in anyway, and what you'll do instead when it does, something that makes the day feel set apart.
Then let the plan settle while you breathe.

wordCard.voice: A day of rest: one day a week set apart from work, holy because God rested, and free because no one should be a slave.

orig.note: Hebrew: Sabbath, the weekly day of rest.

carryVoice: Here's the line: rest day, remembered and kept, both at the same time. See you tomorrow.
